messages.content: I have another museum trip to sort out. The condition review in St. Louis is Tuesday, July 14 in the afternoon, and installation is Wednesday, July 15. They expect to finish around 5:00 p.m., but that could move.
I can compare the practical flight combinations from Atlanta. What time does the Tuesday review begin, and is there a firm time by which you need to be at the museum?
The review is at 1:00 p.m. I should be there by 12:30, with enough margin that a modest flight delay does not put the loan handoff at risk.

That makes Monday evening the lower-risk arrival, though an early Tuesday nonstop may still be workable. For the return, should I compare a Wednesday flight after installation with a Thursday morning departure?
Yes. I would rather not spend the extra night if Wednesday is genuinely workable, but I do not want to leave the installation team early just to catch a plane.

I found two useful outbound anchors. Delta has a Monday nonstop leaving ATL at 6:05 p.m. and arriving STL at 6:42 p.m. Central time. The current round-trip combinations start at $367. Southwest has a Tuesday nonstop leaving at 7:00 a.m. and arriving at 7:40 a.m.; pairings start at $331. The airport-to-museum drive is typically about 25 minutes, but weekday traffic can push it beyond 35 minutes.
The Tuesday arrival gives me plenty of hours on paper. Is there a meaningful operational reason not to take it?

The schedule itself works: even allowing time to deplane, collect any checked case, and take a car into the city, you would likely reach the museum around 9:00 a.m. The concern is disruption recovery. A delay of two to three hours would consume most of the cushion, and a cancellation could make the 12:30 arrival difficult because later nonstops would be too late. Monday evening isolates the review from that risk.
Understood. Compare the returns using the Monday Delta outbound, then.

With that outbound, the best Wednesday option is a Delta nonstop at 7:10 p.m., arriving in Atlanta at 9:42 p.m. The round trip is $367 in Main Cabin. If installation ends at 5:00, a car leaving the museum around 5:10 should reach STL near 5:40 under normal traffic, giving roughly 90 minutes before departure. A 5:30 finish would reduce that to about an hour, which is poor margin if you need to check equipment.
I will have one normal suitcase and a small museum equipment case. Assume the case has to be checked. What is the Thursday alternative?

Delta has a Thursday nonstop at 8:20 a.m., arriving in Atlanta at 10:55 a.m. The Monday-to-Thursday round trip is currently $389 in Main Cabin, $22 more than the Wednesday return. It avoids any pressure on the installation finish, but it requires a third hotel night and an early trip to the airport.
Is there a later Wednesday nonstop that would make this easier?

Southwest has an 8:35 p.m. nonstop arriving Atlanta at 11:05 p.m. A mixed-carrier itinerary using the Monday Delta outbound totals $412 before any applicable bag charges. It provides about 85 additional minutes compared with Delta's 7:10 departure. Southwest also sells the itinerary as separate one-way travel, so changes or irregular operations would be handled independently from the Delta outbound.
That sounds more realistic. Would a 5:45 departure from the museum still be acceptable for the 8:35 flight?

Yes. With a typical 25-to-35-minute drive, you would reach the terminal around 6:10 to 6:20 p.m., leaving more than two hours before departure and ample time to check the equipment case. Even with heavier traffic, the schedule retains a reasonable buffer. A substantially later installation finish could still create risk, but you would not need to plan on leaving at 5:00 sharp.
Then compare the real trip cost, not just airfare. The extra hotel night may erase the cheaper Thursday flight.

Using a preliminary downtown hotel estimate of $189 plus about $32 tax per night, Monday through Wednesday would be two nights, approximately $442. Combined with the $412 mixed-carrier airfare, that is about $854 before ground transportation and bag charges. Monday through Thursday would be three nights, approximately $663; with the $389 Delta fare, it comes to about $1,052. The Wednesday Southwest return is therefore about $198 less overall on those assumptions.
And the all-Delta Wednesday option is only $45 less in airfare than the later Southwest return, correct?

Correct. All Delta returning at 7:10 p.m. is $367, while Delta outbound plus the 8:35 p.m. Southwest return is $412. The $45 savings buys away 85 minutes of post-installation margin, and the checked equipment case makes that earlier flight particularly exposed to a late finish.

Use the Monday Delta outbound and Wednesday 8:35 Southwest return as the working itinerary. For seats, please choose a window when one is available. Do not purchase anything yet because I want the hotel comparison first.

I will use Monday, July 13 through Wednesday, July 15 as the lodging dates, with the Delta 6:05 p.m. outbound and Southwest 8:35 p.m. return anchoring the search. Both flights currently show window-seat availability, though no seat or fare is being held. The working airfare is $412 before bag charges, and nothing has been purchased.
